sharedMechanismsView.label: Deterministic outbound-network egress gate with SSRF/private-range blocking
sharedMechanismsView.description: QM's src/egress-authz-main.ts runs a standalone HTTP CONNECT-style authorization proxy: capability-token-gated, blocks link-local/loopback/cloud-metadata ranges via node:net BlockList, re-resolves the hostname via DNS and re-checks the resolved IP (not just the literal string) against the block-list and policy before allowing the connection, and records every decision to an audit sink. AGW's examples/traffic-egress-proxy demonstrates the same problem class as an actual HTTP CONNECT proxy with hostname allowlisting via TLS SNI (no decryption) or optional TLS termination for HTTP-policy inspection.
sharedMechanismsView.existingCvfOwnerEvidence: EXTENSIONS/CVF_v1.6_AGENT_PLATFORM/cvf-web/src/lib/agent-tools.tsx (tool implementation) + agent-tools.test.tsx:140-173 (SSRF test suite: blocks localhost, 127.0.0.1, 10.x, 192.168.x, 172.16-31.x, 169.254.x.x literal-string/literal-IP forms in the requested URL)
sharedMechanismsView.missingCvfLink: CVF's existing test suite (agent-tools.test.tsx) covers only URLs whose host component is already a literal private/link-local IP string. It does not cover a hostname that RESOLVES to a private/link-local/metadata IP (DNS rebinding) -- QM's egress-authz-main.ts explicitly performs the lookup-then-recheck-resolved-IP step (decide() function, lines 96-123) that CVF's tests give no evidence of.
sharedMechanismsView.expectedBenefit: If CVF's agent-tools.tsx URL check is host-string-only (not verified further in this bounded pass -- the implementation file itself was not opened, only its test file), a DNS-rebinding gap could let an attacker-controlled hostname resolve to a blocked IP at request time and bypass a string-only allow/deny check.
sharedMechanismsView.nextAction: Open agent-tools.tsx's actual URL-validation implementation (not just its test file) in a follow-up pass to confirm whether resolved-IP re-checking already exists; this audit does not claim the gap is proven, only that the test evidence does not demonstrate resolved-IP protection.
sharedMechanismsView.reopenTrigger: A named CVF consumer or security reviewer requests SSRF/DNS-rebinding hardening evidence for agent-initiated outbound fetches

sharedMechanismsView.label: Deterministic shell-command safety policy with de-obfuscation
sharedMechanismsView.description: QM's src/policy/command-policy.ts implements a full command-policy engine: org-floor denylist rules (recursive delete, force-push, destructive SQL, fork bombs, pipe-to-shell) plus scope-composable custom rules, and -- the substantial part -- a scannableCommand() normalizer that recursively unwraps nested shell constructs (command substitution $()/`` `` `, heredocs that run an interpreter, piped producer/consumer pairs, here-strings, simple variable expansion, SQL client -c/-e payload extraction for psql/mysql/sqlite3/etc.) before running regex rules against the fully de-obfuscated scannable text, specifically to prevent quoting/substitution tricks from hiding a destructive pattern from a naive regex scan.
sharedMechanismsView.existingCvfOwnerEvidence: NOT_FOUND in this bounded pass. CVF's SAF1 (docs/reference/CVF_ERH_SAF1_SAFETY_WORKFLOW_CHAIN_2026-06-04.md) is a prompt-text pattern screen (governance-bypass phrase detection), not a shell-command safety/de-obfuscation engine; DLP (dlp-filter-core.ts) is a PII-redaction regex engine, not a command-safety scanner. Neither owner inspects or de-obfuscates a shell command string for destructive-operation patterns.

sharedMechanismsView.label: Non-extractable shared-credential proxy (broker pattern)
sharedMechanismsView.description: QM's skills-seed/use-shared-credential/SKILL.md documents (and names a corresponding core-side broker endpoint, not itself opened) a pattern where the agent never receives a raw shared secret: it names a credential slug, method, URL and headers, and a core-side broker stamps the real secret onto the outbound request, returning only the upstream status/body envelope. The broker enforces per-credential host/method/path-prefix allowlisting and records every use for attribution/billing/abuse review. A parallel path handles Git smart-HTTP remotes without ever placing a token in a clone URL.
sharedMechanismsView.existingCvfOwnerEvidence: NOT_FOUND in this bounded pass. CVF's provider API-key handling (route.ts apiKeyMap, lines ~270-278 per the prior AGW-UC-02 pass) reads keys directly from server-side environment variables and uses them directly server-side for CVF's own first-party provider calls; this is a different shape of problem (CVF's server already holds the keys and never hands them to an agent) rather than QM's shape (an agent-facing broker so a semi-trusted agent process never sees an org's shared third-party secret it would otherwise need to hold locally).
